title: The strong CP problem: why QCD preserves CP
bottleneck: Quantum chromodynamics naturally contains a CP-violating theta term that should generate a neutron electric dipole moment some ten orders of magnitude above current limits, yet measurements show theta is smaller than 10^-10. Nothing in the Standard Model explains why this parameter is essentially zero.
why_it_blocks: An unexplained parameter tuned to one part in ten billion is among the most severe fine-tunings in physics and a standing invitation to new physics, most famously the axion.
current_state: The Peccei-Quinn mechanism and its axion remain the leading solution and drive a global experimental program, but alternatives like massless up quarks or CP as a spontaneously broken symmetry are not fully excluded. Neutron electric dipole moment searches keep improving, and any nonzero signal would immediately falsify the simplest axion-free explanations.
